nodes.name: Abolish Article Nine
nodes.description: A ratified amendment removes Article 9 and establishes a revised constitutional basis for defence.
nodes.effects:
Remove Article 9 and Self-Defence (+5% stability factor, −10% recruitable population factor, −5% army attack). Add Revised Defence Constitution: army attack +5%, recruitable population factor +5%, stability factor −7%, army personnel expenditure +10%.

For 730 days, US opinion of Japan −15 and Soviet opinion of Japan −30. Each government receives its own response:
• United States — Protest: US opinion of Japan becomes −25. Seek safeguards: US opinion becomes −5 and Japan may accept or refuse cooperation; acceptance costs each country $1 billion and grants each navy organisation +3% for 730 days.
• Soviet Union — Condemn: Soviet opinion of Japan becomes −45 and Soviet war support +3 percentage points. Guarded dialogue: Soviet opinion becomes −20 and Soviet treasury −$1 billion.

No treaty, base or nuclear policy changes automatically.
nodes.ownership: Constitutional effects are permanent where specified; temporary effects expire as listed. Costs and votes occur once.
nodes.gate: Requires the referendum, Article 9 and Self-Defence, and stability ≥55%. Stability is the proposed public-mandate proxy, not the referendum vote percentage.

nodes.name: Confirm Article Nine
nodes.description: The referendum rejects abolition, preserving Article 9 as the constitutional basis of Japanese security policy.
nodes.effects: Retain Article 9 and Self-Defence: stability factor +5%, recruitable population factor −10%, army attack −5%. Political power +50; stability factor +3% for 730 days. The American and Soviet reactions to abolition do not occur.
nodes.ownership: Constitutional effects are permanent where specified; temporary effects expire as listed. Costs and votes occur once.
nodes.gate: Requires the referendum and Article 9 and Self-Defence.
